descriptionChirho: Qal intransitive: to become many, multiply, increase in number — the subject itself grows numerous (Arabic kathura/yakthuru, Korean 많아지다, Swahili -ongezeka).
Qal imperative: command to multiply and become numerous, as in the creation mandate 'be fruitful and multiply' (Arabic ukthuru, Korean 많아지라/불어나라, Swahili -ongezekeni).

Hifil causative: to make many, cause to multiply, increase something or someone in number — the subject causes another to become numerous (Arabic akthara/yukathiru, Korean 많게 하다, Swahili -zidisha/-ongeza).

labelChirho: much, many, exceedingly (Hifil infinitive absolute as adverb)
descriptionChirho: Hifil infinitive absolute used adverbially: much, many, very, exceedingly, greatly — modifies another verb to indicate intensity or abundance (Arabic kathiran, Korean 많이/심히/크게, Swahhi sana/mengi/nyingi).

labelChirho: from multiplying (Hifil infinitive construct with prep)
descriptionChirho: Hifil infinitive construct with preposition min: from multiplying, indicating source or prevention of the act of making many (Arabic min ikthari, Korean 로부터/많아짐, Swahili kutoka kuongezeka).
Piel intensive: to rear, bring up, nurture children or young — a distinct semantic domain of child-rearing rather than numerical increase (Arabic rabba/yurabbi, Korean 키우다, Swahili -lea).

To make great or magnify a person, used of God magnifying a human or of enlarging territory — semantic shift from numerical increase to qualitative greatness (Arabic azzama/kabbara, Korean 크게 하다, Swahili -fanya mkuu).

labelChirho: be great, be far/too much (Qal stative)
descriptionChirho: Qal stative or imperfect with sense of being great in size or distance, or being too much/excessive — distinct from numerical multiplication (Arabic tala/yakburu, Korean 크다/멀다, Swahili -kubwa/-refu).

Hifil imperative or infinitive used adverbially with another verb to mean thoroughly or abundantly — the multiplying action modifies the main verb's intensity (Arabic ighsilni = wash me thoroughly, Korean 씻으소서, Swahili nioshe).
